verses.text: For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph. I cry out to God. I cry out to God for help, and he listens to me.
When I was in trouble, I looked for the Lord. All night I lifted my hands in prayer without getting tired. But nothing could comfort me.
I think of God, and I groan. I think about it, and my spirit grows weak. Selah.
You keep my eyes from closing. I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
I think about the old days, the years long ago.
At night I remember my songs. I think deeply, and my spirit asks questions:
"Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he never be kind to us again?
Has his faithful love disappeared forever? Has his promise failed for all time?
Has God forgotten to be kind? Has his anger shut off his mercy?" Selah.
Then I thought, "This is what hurts me most: that the Most High no longer uses his right hand for us."
But I will remember what the LORD has done. I will remember the amazing things you did long ago.
I will think about all your works and consider all your mighty acts.
God, your ways are holy. What god is as great as our God?
You are the God who does amazing things. You show your strength among the nations.
With your strong arm you rescued your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God. The waters saw you and trembled. The deepest seas shook.
The clouds poured down rain. The skies rumbled with thunder. Your arrows of lightning flashed everywhere.
Your thunder roared in the whirlwind. Your lightning lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook.
Your path went through the sea, your way through the mighty waters, but no one saw your footprints.
You led your people like a flock of sheep, using Moses and Aaron.
